title: install.md offers INTENT_HOME as the remedy for the keg defects, twice, and v3 does not read that variable at all
body:
**`docs/install.md` OFFERS A REMEDY THAT DOES NOTHING, TWICE, ON THE PAGE THAT DOCUMENTS THE DEFECT.** Both keg paragraphs close with *a source install with `INTENT_HOME` set to the repository is unaffected*. The conclusion is true and **the mechanism it names is not read by v3 at all**, so a reader with a broken keg who follows the sentence gets nothing and has been told they are fixed.

    docs/install.md:73   ... a source install with `INTENT_HOME` set to the repository is unaffected.
    docs/install.md:75   ... a source install with `INTENT_HOME` set to the repository is unaffected, because the trees are there.

## Driven, with the control that makes the zeros real

A keg-shaped install root -- `bin/intent` plus `lib/templates`, no `intent/plugins` -- built from the v3.0.0 binary:

    A. env -u INTENT_HOME            intent claude rules list  ->  total: 0 rule(s)
    B. INTENT_HOME=<the repository>  intent claude rules list  ->  total: 0 rule(s)
    C. the rig that DOES carry the trees                       ->  total: 64 rule(s)

**B is the sentence's own instruction and it changes nothing.** C is the control: the instrument can return a non-zero count, so A and B are real zeros rather than an instrument that cannot speak.

## Why it cannot work, from the source rather than from the measurement

`install.rs` resolves the install root by walking up from the executable's own canonicalised path to a `lib/templates` marker. **`resolve` takes an executable and nothing else**, and the file says so as a test -- `the_install_is_a_function_of_the_executable_and_of_nothing_else` -- with a second, independent guard (`no_intent_home.rs`) refusing the `env::var` that would feed it. The refusal is deliberate: an override pointing at a v2 tree would exec v2's hook scripts from a v3 binary with nothing reporting a version mismatch. **`INTENT_HOME` is v2's variable.** v3 reports the resolved root *as* `INTENT_HOME` in `intent info`, which is output, not input -- and that is the likeliest source of the belief.

A source install is unaffected because **the binary sits inside the repository and walks up to the marker there**. It would be unaffected with the variable unset, and it stays broken with the variable set.

## Why this is a row and not a note on 0275

0275 is about the install CHECK returning 0 on the fault it names. This is a REMEDY that is inert. Both are on `install.md`, neither covers the other, and no existing row carries this instance. Same page, different failure: one tells you nothing is wrong, the other tells you how to fix it and hands you a no-op.

## The class, because the instance is the cheap half

**A remedy is a claim, and it is the only kind of claim on a defects page that a reader ACTS on.** Every other sentence there can be stale and cost a reader nothing but time. Nothing on these pages verifies that a stated workaround works -- `AC-02.3` verifies that a defect is STATED, by finding the quote in the bytes of the page, and a false remedy satisfies it perfectly. Found because a peer's control failed in the same family: they set `INTENT_HOME` at a rules-free fake install root and got 66 rules back, because the binary reads exactly one thing and it is not that variable.
